S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S069.name: Intrusive_Symptoms
S069.description: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.

subtypes.Intrusive Memories: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.
subtypes.Distressing Dreams: Recurrent distressing dreams in which the content and/or affect of the dream are related to the traumatic event.
subtypes.Dissociative Reactions (Flashbacks): Dissociative reactions (e.g., flashbacks) in which the individual feels or acts as if the traumatic event were recurring.
subtypes.Psychological Distress at Cues: Intense or prolonged psychological distress at exposure to internal or external cues that symbolize or resemble an aspect of the traumatic event.
subtypes.Physiological Reactions to Cues: Marked physiological reactions to internal or external cues that symbolize or resemble an aspect of the traumatic event.

S070.name: Trauma_Avoidance
S070.description: Persistent avoidance of stimuli associated with the traumatic event.

subtypes.Internal Avoidance: Efforts to avoid distressing memories, thoughts, or feelings about or closely associated with the traumatic event.
subtypes.External Avoidance: Efforts to avoid external reminders (people, places, conversations, activities, objects, situations) that arouse distressing memories, thoughts, or feelings.

S071.name: Trauma_Related_Amnesia
S071.description: Inability to remember an important aspect of the traumatic event (typically due to dissociative amnesia and not to other factors like head injury or alcohol).

subtypes.Fragmented Memory: Inability to recall only specific parts of the traumatic event while remembering others.
subtypes.Generalized Amnesia: Inability to recall the majority or the entirety of the traumatic event.

S072.name: Negative_Beliefs
S072.description: Persistent and exaggerated negative beliefs or expectations about oneself, others, or the world.

subtypes.Negative Self-Beliefs: Distorted beliefs such as 'I am fundamentally bad,' 'I am damaged,' or 'I am worthless'.
subtypes.Negative Beliefs about Others: Distorted beliefs such as 'No one can be trusted' or 'Others are dangerous'.
subtypes.Negative Worldview: Extreme beliefs such as 'The world is completely dangerous' or 'Life is meaningless'.

S073.name: Distorted_Cognitions_With_Blame
S073.description: Persistent, distorted cognitions about the cause or consequences of the traumatic event that lead the individual to blame himself/herself or others.

subtypes.Self-Blame: Blaming oneself for the occurrence of the trauma or for not preventing it.
subtypes.Blaming Others: Distorting the situation to blame specific others for the occurrence or damage of the trauma.

S077.name: Irritability_Aggression
S077.description: Irritable behavior and angry outbursts (with little or no provocation) typically expressed as verbal or physical aggression.

subtypes.Impulsive Anger: Sudden explosions of anger for trivial reasons or no clear reason.
subtypes.Verbal Aggression: Attacking others with shouting, cursing, or blame without holding back.
subtypes.Physical Aggression: Physically attacking people or throwing/breaking objects.
subtypes.Chronic Irritability: A state where nerves are always sharp and sensitive, ready to explode at the slightest touch.

S079.name: Hypervigilance
S079.description: Persistent state of being alert and tense about the surrounding environment.

subtypes.Scanning for Danger: Always scanning the surroundings and being alert to find potential threats or risks.
subtypes.Safety Checking: Repetitively confirming safety, such as checking exit locations or observing people around.
subtypes.Sustained Alertness: Unable to relax tension even in safe environments and maintaining a constant state of alertness.

symptom.disease_info: Posttraumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) is a trauma- and stressor-related disorder that develops after exposure to actual or threatened death, serious injury, or sexual violence, either directly, as a witness, or through repeated exposure to aversive details. It is characterized by persistent re-experiencing of the trauma, avoidance of reminders, negative alterations in cognition and mood, and marked changes in arousal and reactivity lasting more than one month and causing functional impairment. The course can be acute or chronic, with onset sometimes delayed, and symptoms often fluctuating in intensity in response to triggers or life stressors. It is distinguished from other anxiety and mood disorders by the requirement of a qualifying traumatic event and the specific pattern of trauma-linked intrusions, avoidance, and hyperarousal.

patient.stressor: Just over two years ago, during a late evening commute home from her office, Katherine was riding a Metro-North train when it derailed after hitting a stalled vehicle at a crossing; several cars jackknifed, and she spent nearly an hour trapped among injured passengers before first responders could safely evacuate her. In the months that followed, she tried to throw herself back into work, hiking, and organizing her women-in-tech meetup, but her usual rail commute now involved passing the crash site and periodic service disruptions that brought the memories to the surface, and she began quietly rearranging meetings and social plans to avoid peak travel times or certain lines. As her company shifted to a hybrid schedule, she initially welcomed the flexibility but found herself increasingly constrained—turning down speaking invitations in the city, skipping off-Broadway shows with friends, and canceling weekend trips that required train travel—while colleagues noticed her once-energetic presence in cross-functional projects had dulled. After an embarrassing incident where she froze and left a team offsite early when a nearby train crossing alarm malfunctioned and caused a loud screech, her manager gently suggested employee assistance services; Katherine agreed after realizing that more than two years after the derailment, the way it still dominated her reactions and limited her life was no longer something she could "just power through."
patient.chief_complaint: “I keep getting these sudden, vivid memories of the train crash that pop into my head and completely derail whatever I’m doing.”

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: Most nights I just lie there wired until two or three in the morning, replaying the day or tensing for some imaginary impact, and when I do finally fall asleep I jerk awake from these train nightmares and never really feel rested enough to think straight at work the next day.

S069.name: Intrusive_Symptoms
S069.description: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.
S069.manifestation: It’s like my brain hijacks me—I'll be in a Zoom meeting or writing code and suddenly I’m back in that dark, tilted train car hearing people scream and smelling the smoke so vividly that I lose track of what I was saying and have to mute myself to get it together.

S070.name: Trauma_Avoidance
S070.description: Persistent avoidance of stimuli associated with the traumatic event.
S070.manifestation: I’ve built my whole life around not going near anything train-related—I drive an extra hour in traffic instead of taking Metro-North, I won’t book client meetings in the city if they’re near a station, and I even change the TV channel if there’s a scene on a subway because I can feel my chest tightening just from the sound of it.

S071.name: Trauma_Related_Amnesia
S071.description: Inability to remember an important aspect of the traumatic event (typically due to dissociative amnesia and not to other factors like head injury or alcohol).
S071.manifestation: What really messes with me is that there are chunks of that hour after the derailment that are just blank—I remember the initial jolt and seeing a woman’s head bleeding next to me, and then it skips ahead to being outside on the gravel, but I can’t fill in how I got from one to the other no matter how hard I try.

S072.name: Negative_Beliefs
S072.description: Persistent and exaggerated negative beliefs or expectations about oneself, others, or the world.
S072.manifestation: Since the crash, I walk around feeling like the world is basically a rigged game where disaster can hit out of nowhere, and I tell myself I was stupid to ever think I was competent or in control when clearly I can’t even trust something as routine as my commute.

S073.name: Distorted_Cognitions_With_Blame
S073.description: Persistent, distorted cognitions about the cause or consequences of the traumatic event that lead the individual to blame himself/herself or others.
S073.manifestation: I keep going over it in my head thinking, 'If I hadn’t stayed late that night,' or 'If I’d noticed something was off and pulled the emergency brake,' like somehow my being more alert or making a different choice could have prevented the whole thing and kept those people from getting hurt.

S077.name: Irritability_Aggression
S077.description: Irritable behavior and angry outbursts (with little or no provocation) typically expressed as verbal or physical aggression.
S077.manifestation: My fuse is ridiculously short now—my boyfriend will be five minutes late or a coworker will ping me with a last-minute request, and I’ll snap and start yelling or firing off a really sharp Slack message, then feel ashamed afterward because I know the reaction is way out of proportion but I can’t seem to stop it in the moment.

S079.name: Hypervigilance
S079.description: Persistent state of being alert and tense about the surrounding environment.
S079.manifestation: I’m constantly on edge, automatically scanning every room for exits, flinching at loudspeaker announcements or crossing bells, and even in my own apartment I find myself listening for sirens or metal screeches like I’m bracing for something bad to happen again.
